title: WHO: Drowning Among Top Causes of Death in Children

image.attribution: Vic Brincat from Keswick, Ontario, Canada / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-2.0

main_content:
The World Health Organization (WHO) says drowning is among the top five causes of death for children under the age of 15.

The United Nations agency also found that boys and girls living near open water sources, are especially at risk.

Children in Asia are especially at risk in extreme heat during the summer and during the rainy season.

The Asia-based group Alliance for Safe Children says drowning rates in developing countries are 10 to 20 times higher than those in developed countries.

Bill Kirby of Australia won a gold medal as a swimmer in the 2000 Olympics. He now leads swimming classes and training programs in Asia, mainly in Indonesia and Malaysia.

Kirby told VOA that governments and swimming organizations can work together to campaign for improved water safety. “One of the first steps is actually to create a national body that looks after water safety.”

options: Asia during extreme heat and rainy season
questions.answer: Asia during extreme heat and rainy season

options: A former athlete promoting safe swimming practices

questions.question: What is the first step to improve water safety?
options: To conduct swimming lessons for children
To create a national body that oversees water safety
To build more swimming pools in urban areas
To increase advertising about water hazards
questions.answer: To create a national body that oversees water safety
